account:
Today I have been following my appointments, but much of the conversation around town concerns bread, grain, and an unverified bridge or port change. At the mill I saw eighty hay bales offered at two emeralds each. There appears to be stock available, while people have reported difficulty paying for it. Neighbour heard the innkeeper ask builder about grain credit and selling authorized spare planks to buy nineteen bales. I personally saw builder give planks to baker at 11:26, but I did not see grain bought or learn the terms of that transfer. I heard that the innkeeper carried a sack of bread; that does not prove a grain purchase. The baker reportedly filled a large bread order, and freight says the baker has been arranging supplies privately with customers. My tentative interpretation is that people are arranging trades or credit to obtain food, not necessarily changing public policy.

Several people have repeated a bridge or port rumour involving the bakery, baker, innkeeper, and freight, but nobody I have spoken with has verified an actual change. I should not treat repetition as confirmation. Freight has requested a ferry and warehouse operations discussion this evening, alongside or following the already approved eighteen-hundred great hall lighting inspection. That may clarify transport matters, but I do not yet know of any concrete proposal or hidden purpose.

The missing town account figures remain unresolved. Secretary reports no council correspondence, no decisions awaiting me, and no reliable lead identifying who holds the accounts. Earlier searches found no council records in the great hall table chests. This is an unresolved administrative concern, not evidence against any particular person.

I am at neighbour's cottage for tea. Neighbour has been welcoming and careful to distinguish hearsay from facts, and is now asking how I am rather than discussing business. I need to return to the office for sixteen-thirty. The quiet visit itself has been a pleasant part of the day.
